firm_judgment.decision: No substantiated upgrade from conditional moderate LONG at $52.25. No substantiated SHORT. Intel remains a researched recovery candidate, but a demonstrable price advantage is not established. If selecting afresh specifically for a strong differentiated mispricing pitch, this record does not yet justify selecting Intel over alternatives; this is not a claim that Intel cannot outperform.
firm_judgment.concrete_thesis_that_survives: Server demand, richer CPU content and additional qualified output can let DCAI profit outweigh PC weakness. At $52.25 that business recovery is already required by the forecast: unchanged funded economics produce $51.07 December 2026 APV and $77.46 December 2030 value, about 9.94% conditional annual price appreciation. The live debate is whether strong customer economics and manufacturing recovery persist long enough to earn that return, not whether servers can grow at all.
firm_judgment.sharpened_variant: Our 2027 operating trajectory is more optimistic than the directly published iFAST forecast and strains the public S&P aggregate revenue proxy. A marketwide underappreciation claim remains unproved: major professional research already recognizes the server recovery, and our own fair-value calculation gives no material price cushion.
why_no_stronger_long: More confidence in near-term capacity can make an existing forecast more credible without increasing intrinsic value. The unchanged $51.07 planning APV is 2.26% below $52.25 and already assumes successful recovery.

92.3% of December 2026 operating value lies after 2030; near-term LTAs or 2027 wafer output do not secure these cash flows. The decisive missing evidence is persistence of consolidated profits and capital returns, not another short-term shipment sensitivity.

The model already includes 40% mature DCAI margin, 2030-40 CPU revenue growth of 6% annually, 0.8 incremental capital productivity and a funded 3% perpetuity. The resulting roughly 23.5% incremental terminal NOPAT/net investment is an assumed economic rent, not a measured moat.
Historical cost learning is in Q3 economics and the subsequent Foundry profit path. Internal transfer-price changes cannot create group profit twice.

The model already contains gross external packaging revenue of $7B by 2030 with $5.5B capital through 2030, plus Other DCAI of $17.44B. Commercial announcements must exceed these expectations after costs and overlap to create extra value.

Cash claims and known collateral treatment are already reconciled. No newly substantiated uncounted asset, contractual cash stream or removable capital obligation was found that closes the price issue.
why_no_short: Approximately fair modeled value is not overvaluation adequate to establish a short.

Revenue, consolidated gross profit, demand and capacity investment support a plausible recovery. No source demonstrates permanent loss or supply failure sufficient to make the downside path the best forecast.

Public target surveys and the two directly published research valuations are above $52.25, but their differing scopes and methods do not prove upside either. They make a simplistic consensus-blind short story especially unconvincing.
Lower-demand and joint-downside outputs are conditional states, not estimated probabilities. Converting them into a short target solely to improve pitch contrast would tune direction to rhetoric.
evidence_needed_to_cross_the_price_gap: A buyer-specific, economically distinct contracted volume, price and capital arrangement extending beyond the already modeled program, reconciled to group cash and existing forecast overlap.

Evidence of repeat qualified CPU purchases at retained net prices plus corresponding package/manufacturing costs after supply normalization, sufficient to defend a durable segment and consolidated margin.
A credible jointly funded capital and operating path beyond 2030 that supports the embedded growth and economic returns. Capacity announcements and same-core prices do not identify this path.
A lower actual entry can improve the unchanged conditional return: $48.3801944 gives 12% to the same 2030 target. It does not improve business quality or turn a weak forecast into a sound one.
firm_judgment.not_required_to_make_a_legitimate_long: A long need not meet an invented 12% or 15% minimum, prove a proprietary information edge, or be below every analyst forecast. The issue is the strength of evidence relative to the risk and purchase price. A roughly 10% return is not inherently invalid; it simply cannot be sold as a measured expectation or obvious mispricing.
firm_judgment.recommended_pitch_change: Replace the implication of an isolated pre-earnings comparator with an explicitly dated current-forecast panel: iFAST FY2027 growth comparison plus S&P non-Products headroom. Use the refreshed $52.25 entry with unchanged $51.07 planning value and $77.46 target; retain moderate conviction. Say exactly why the owned forecast may be right and acknowledge that evidence improves forecast defensibility more than present value. Do not raise the target, lower the risk rate, assign unobserved scenario weights, import analyst targets, or label already modeled packaging as a free option.

current_consolidated_consensus_proxy.interpretation: Our Products forecast alone consumes 98.65% of the current consolidated consensus proxy. It leaves $0.94B for external Foundry and external All Other, whereas our modeled All Other proxy is $2.8B and gross packaging is $0.5B. This is a headroom diagnostic showing the optimistic direction of our forecast. It is not a fully matched revenue beat: legacy external Foundry and future Other eliminations are unspecified.
current_consolidated_consensus_proxy.completion_needed: Own explicit legacy external Foundry and Other-internal series before publishing consolidated revenue comparisons. Do not quietly insert a residual to hit consensus.

ifast_same_period_growth.caution: Different forecast bases are incompletely disclosed. Relative optimism is observed; a dollar beat cannot be derived by multiplying their rate by our base.
